report.answer_text:
Cigarette adverts were banned from UK television on 1 August 1965. Adverts for loose tobacco and cigars continued until 1991, when they were outlawed under the Broadcasting Act 1990.[1]
Background: A 1950 British Medical Journal report had suggested a link between smoking and lung cancer. By 1962 the Royal College of Physicians had enough evidence to push for an advertising ban.[2]
Legal basis: One source says the ban came under the Television Act 1964, and an EU directive in the 1980s reinforced it.[3]
Aftermath: Tobacco companies moved heavily into sports sponsorship after the ban. They wanted to get round it and still get a free plug in front of a mass TV audience.[1]
